5533228304.body:
Coordination note — this overlaps #559 on the same surface, and the two should be sequenced deliberately.

Both touch `ix-cli/src/cli/__tests__/unresolved-machine-output.test.ts` (the only shared file; whichever merges second needs a rebase there), and both flip the same behavior class: a non-zero exit on an unresolved target where the command previously exited 0 with a null result (#546 here, #539 there).

#559 is a draft on purpose and names the reason: its exit-code flip is a breaking change for machine consumers, and it is sequenced as step 2 after three plugin PRs land (ix-opencode-plugin#20, ix-openclaw-plugin#33, ix-claude-plugin#37) precisely so those consumers are ready for the non-zero before it ships. This PR's 8-command flip is the same breaking-change class — if it merges ahead of those consumers, the degradation #559 is carefully sequencing around can arrive through a different door.

Suggestions: reference #559 in the body so reviewers see the overlap; rebase the shared test file against whichever lands first; and if any of the three plugin consumers call these graph commands, land this PR in the same order #559 uses (plugins first).

5549703398.body:
The ambiguity fix is right — `5280ec6` puts `process.exitCode = 1` in `reportResolutionFailure` so both arms agree, and the two tests now pin `toBe(1)` where they pinned `toBeUndefined()`. That closes my finding, including the out-of-range `--pick` case, which was the one I thought hardest to defend at exit 0.

**I have merged every other open PR on this repo today and deliberately left this one open.** Not because of anything in the code — because your own merge gate is still open upstream, and I checked rather than assumed:

| consumer | state |
|---|---|
| `ix-opencode-plugin` #20, #21 | **MERGED** |
| `ix-openclaw-plugin` #33 | **OPEN** |
| `ix-claude-plugin` #37, #38 | **OPEN** |

Two of the three still treat a non-zero exit as a failure and discard the body. Landing this now would ship the exit-code flip for eight graph commands ahead of them — which is the same shape as the bug I reported inside this PR (the in-repo MCP server discarding a well-formed record because `!result.ok`), just in consumers we do not control from here. You fixed the in-repo one; the external ones are what is left.

So this is ready on the merits and waiting on those three PRs, exactly as you and @Alot1z sequenced it. Once `ix-openclaw-plugin#33` and `ix-claude-plugin#37`/`#38` land, this should go straight in — I do not have any open findings against it.

One residual, small and out of scope for this PR, recorded so it is not lost: `resolveFileOrEntity` (`resolve.ts:692`) still calls `reportAmbiguousTarget` directly with a hardcoded `"text"` and sets no exit code, so `ix locate` keeps exiting 0 on an ambiguous target. That is #559's surface rather than this one's, and #559 is a draft behind the same three plugin PRs — worth folding into it there.

## For context on what changed underneath you

`main` moved a long way today: #570, #577, #578, #582, #583, #584, #587, #589, #590, #591, #592, #593–#596, #597, #598, #601 and #602 all landed. This branch is still `MERGEABLE`, but expect to want a rebase before it goes in — `ci-success` now requires six jobs (`api-parity`, `doc-parity`, `links` and two harness smoke jobs joined the original three), and `docs/` gained a committed flag reference plus a dead-link gate that will check any URL you add.
